newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Some Hungarian state firms can't be sold - minister.
newsitem.headline: Some Hungarian state firms can't be sold - minister.

text.p: Hungary is realising it will not be able to sell some state-owned firms because of a lack of investor interest, the privatisation minister said on Monday.

"There will be quite a few companies that will remain state property despite our intentions to the contrary, after the privatisation process is completed at the end of this year ," Judit Csiha told a trade union conference. "We will have to decide what to do with them."

Despite its success with privatisations, which have brought over 900 billion forints ($5.3 billion) to the cash-strapped government's coffers this decade, Hungary has had difficulties selling some, mostly smallish companies.

The state privatisation agency APV Rt has repeatedly come up with new methods to sell these firms, including a scheme under which small and medium-sized firms were sold at simple auctions, without the APV's usual bureaucratic hurdles.

Csiha said that privately-held companies in which the government has a minority stake are a particular problem, as the majority owners have little incentive to buy out the inactive government's shares at a fair value.

In efforts to speed sales, the APV's predecessors often agreed in the early 1990s to deals which gave investors control over firms without having to buy all their shares, and which tied the government's hands alienating its stake.
Csiha said the government is expected to come up with a policy on what to do with the unsellable firms, as well as with firms in which the state wants to retain a stake, sometime in September.
APV wants to maintain various stakes in over 100 companies, including OTP Bank, the oil company MOL and the national airlines MALEV to ensure services vital to the economy are maintained.
Csiha said that it should be examined whether it is necessary to keep stakes in all the over 100 firms, many of which are easily sellable.
Csiha did not indicate how many firms will be hard to sell, but said that in 1997, APV expects to privatise at least 270 of the 554 firms that were in APV's portfolio at the end of 1996.
They will include public utilities still in state hands, pulp and paper firms and state farms, she said, adding that the government hopes to raise 196 billion from sales in 1997. ($1=169.11 Forint)
